title: bug: an observe-path transient git failure wedges the delivery checkout BLOCKED with no recovery proof
description:
Found by worker-1b2cd09b on task-cab96ebcd3b6403cbbf412bdad839403. The following was read at HEAD cdca7094; no test reproduces it yet.

landOne (node-lander.ts:198) reports an observe GIT_FAILED without recording it and says "the next pass retries". In production that is false: repository-delivery-runtime.ts:120 returns RETRY only for GIT_INDEX_LOCKED, so repository-delivery-coordinator.ts:174 calls block(). BLOCKED has no transitions. Recovery needs either !everExecuted or a durable refusal receipt, and this path has neither, so the checkout is held forever and every later node is refused with REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_BUSY.

Parent row task-cab96ebc adds the RETRY edge for transient VERIFICATION codes. Extend that edge to the observe path once the parent lands; both rows edit the same land() line.

Prefer no disk mutation; if unavoidable first inspect exact paths and save live bytes outside tree under task+worker+nonce, record pre-mutation SHA256, restore from that fresh backup, and independently prove restored live hash equals prehash in a separate call, never via git restore or bare diff. In-memory Vite transform only, no repository path written, both guards silent (exactly one disjunct removed, parent's TRANSIENT and index-lock branches provably intact), temp config outside the checkout and deleted.

ATTACKER PASS over the complete two-file diff:
1. DOES A BARE "GIT_FAILED" EVER MEAN POST-EFFECT? This is the disjunct's whole safety premise, so I enumerated producers instead of assuming. `git grep -n '"GIT_FAILED"' -- apps/daemon/src` (non-test) returns FOUR non-test hits: my new predicate line, and git-landing-port.ts :31 (the type), :157 (`status` nonzero), :163 (`hash-object` nonzero), :166 (id-count mismatch) — all three producers are inside `observe()`, which is read-only and runs at node-lander.ts:191, strictly BEFORE `checkLandingVerification`, before `commitJournaledLanding` and before any commit. `grep -n "outcome:" node-lander.ts` confirms landOne's only other outcomes are LANDING_RECEIPT_INVALID, the journal-gate code, NODE_BRIEF_MISSING, "REFUSED"/ledger codes from refuse(), the namespaced VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_* from unrecordedLandingReport, GIT_INDEX_LOCKED (:241) and GIT_COMMIT_FAILED / REPOSITORY_RECOVERY_* (:237) from the commit. None of those is the bare literal. node-lander.ts:139's observe failure belongs to `baseline()`, which flows through the coordinator's baseline callback and never into land()'s `reports`. So the new edge cannot reach a post-effect outcome today. STANDING HAZARD, unchanged by this row but now load-bearing in one more place: the verified-workspace code is NAMESPACED (VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_GIT_FAILED); renaming it to a bare GIT_FAILED would silently join the retry set. The existing census arm "classifies exactly the refusal codes checkLandingVerification can return" pins that table, so such a rename reds there.
2. REPEATED/CONCURRENT ADVANCE CANNOT DUPLICATE A LANDING. `advance()` still holds the `advancing` flag and the per-root `busy` set; `landOne` still returns null when a receipt already exists; `transition`/`release` still take an expectedRevision CAS. RETRY only writes phase back to AWAITING_LANDING. Pinned: a further advance after LANDED moves neither HEAD nor the landing aggregate, and node b then starts ok.
3. A MISSING RECEIPT IS NOT LANDING AUTHORITY. readRepositoryDeliveryFacts maps LANDING_RECEIPT_NOT_FOUND to ACCEPTED, never LANDED; coordinator:169 releases only on LANDED, and the new edge additionally requires `facts === "ACCEPTED"` (coordinator:173, unchanged). Pinned by the exact `{code:"LANDING_RECEIPT_NOT_FOUND", ok:false}` assertion plus node b's REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_BUSY/REPOSITORY_DELIVERY while the retry is owed.
4. A BASELINE OR VERIFICATION FAILURE CANNOT STAND IN FOR OBSERVE. The fault is armed only after facts are ACCEPTED, and `f.tests()` is pinned at 1 through both retries and after the landing — the acceptance is consumed once and never re-minted.
5. POST-INTENT AND RESTART FENCES UNCHANGED. `landingJournalGate` still runs first; the post-intent arm still ends in BLOCKED + BUSY, and the recovery/workflow suites are green.
6. OWNERSHIP VS REVISION. The test compares the whole `handle.owner` (including ownershipToken) and {baselineId, sessionId}, and deliberately does NOT pin `revision` — a retry legitimately advances it. Pinning it would have been a false failure.
7. ALREADY-BLOCKED IS NOT REPAIRED. advanceOne returns immediately for BLOCKED (:130); nothing in the diff touches that. Forward-only fix.

DISCLOSED TRADE-OFF (theoretical, deliberate, DoD-authorized): a PERMANENTLY failing observe — a genuinely broken repository where `git status` never succeeds — now retries once per advance forever instead of wedging BLOCKED on the first failure. That is the same unbounded cadence the pre-existing GIT_INDEX_LOCKED and TRANSIENT branches already use, no retry budget was authorized, and each pass prints `[lander] <node>: GIT_FAILED (<detail>)` so an operator sees it. It is strictly better than the bug it replaces: the old behaviour was terminal BLOCKED with no receipt and no recovery proof, refusing every later node with REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_BUSY forever. Recorded, not fixed — a budget would be new scope.

Other checklist items: no new input surface, resource, handle or subprocess in production (one added boolean disjunct); the test closes the runtime and restores the spy in `finally` on top of the existing afterEach fixture cleanup; no partial-write path introduced. Nothing found that warrants a new implementation row, and no security/evidence row is being filed — per the epic rail this row owns the hardening.

TOU
